solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Report holes being punched in crevice

indicators.note: one thing placed within another, so the jumbled letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: a rift is a crack or fissure

indicators.note: something punched is knocked about and out of shape, so these letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes gaps being knocked into a crack in rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a verb meaning to describe, but it is the noun for a loud bang, like a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp explosive sound of a gun firing, and the crack of a single rifle discharge is exactly that.

clue.text: Solo needing some practice, rarely uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards
'some' asks for only part of the following words, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A soloist who rarely practises needs to be encouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters are read upwards in this down entry: pracTICE Rarely, backwards, gives RECIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A recit, short for recitative, is a passage sung by one voice in opera or oratorio, in the rhythm of speech.

clue.text: Pretending function complicated, shift political camp

parts.note: fancy means elaborate or intricate
a shift is a simple straight dress
a political party is a faction or camp

explanation.surface: A complex role in government is used as cover for changing political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as a job or a mathematical term, but here it means a social gathering; 'Pretending' is the guests dressing up as someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is a formal social event, and at this one guests pretend to be other people by wearing costumes.

clue.text: Flat object's thrown hard for sport

parts.note: flat and even both mean level

indicators.note: to throw something is to cast it away, so a letter is discarded from the word

parts.note: an object is a thing
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A flat thing is hurled with force in some sporting event, like a discus.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in object's means 'has': the object has thrown out H, leaving TING after EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the equestrian competition combining dressage, cross-country riding and show jumping over several days.

clue.text: Considerable fine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: large in amount, as in a generous sum of money
second meaning: good-looking or of fine appearance

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like one phrase about a big penalty, but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome profit is a large one, and a handsome person is attractive, a fine-looking specimen.

clue.text: Quite dark, first of those books for women?

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that initial is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British organisation for women
lit is short for literature, books in general

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether gloomy novels are really aimed at female readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsy: literature for the Women's Institute, a British community group for women famous for jam and choirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes the dim half-light after sunset, when it is not yet fully night but already fairly gloomy.

clue.text: Index finger perhaps where one has a hand?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something used to prod, as a pointing finger can be
second meaning: a card game in which each player holds a hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' tempts you to stay with the body, but the second meaning is a hand of cards in a gambling game.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker is anything that jabs, and a forefinger is used to jab people; the card game deals every player a hand.

clue.text: Spike prodding metal pulled from furnace, very hot

indicators.note: a prodding object pokes into something, so one piece is pushed inside the other

parts.note: pig iron is the crude metal run off from a blast furnace
a pin is a thin pointed spike

explanation.surface: A spike is thrust into glowing metal drawn out of a furnace, still extremely hot.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN pokes into PIG, the name for iron just cast from a blast furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping is used almost only in the phrase piping hot, describing food or liquid so hot it is steaming.

clue.text: A lip-smacking snack?

parts.note: surface reading: a tasty bite to eat that makes you smack your lips
setter's reading: something that literally smacks you in the lips, a punch served up as food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lip-smacking' normally means delicious; read literally it is a blow landing on the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase for a punch in the mouth dresses the blow up as a snack, so a lip-smacking bite fits.

clue.text: Bird basted, roaster cooked after oven cleared out

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or mixed up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
clearing something out removes it entirely, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before the removal
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A bird has been basted and roasted once the oven was emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: Take OAST out of ROASTER to leave RER, then mix it with BASTED. An oast is the hop-drying kiln of Kent, whose oast houses are a familiar sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin redbreast is the traditional British name for the robin, named for its orange-red chest feathers.

clue.text: Staff keeping close to gourmet in French restaurant

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: Employees hover close to a food lover in a Parisian bistro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests restaurant workers, but it is a stick, CANE, which holds T; 'in French' then adds EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a self-service eating place in a workplace, school or barracks, a basic kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Appropriate money, one million up front

parts.note: Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for million
the pound is British money

explanation.surface: A suitable sum is paid, with a million handed over in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective for suitable, but it is the verb meaning to seize; 'up front' puts I and M before the money.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take possession of something, and authorities impound goods or vehicles by seizing them.

clue.text: Judge and godly type meeting

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person

explanation.surface: A judge sits down with a pious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun for the person; it is the verb, TRY, as a court tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is an arranged meeting, usually a secret romantic rendezvous between lovers.

clue.text: A hook at the back splitting top sail

indicators.note: something that splits a thing wedges itself into the middle of it

parts.note: a spinning top is a spinner
taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hook on the rear edge tears the uppermost sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top sail' reads as a topsail, but 'top' is the spinning toy, SPINNER, split by A and K.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is the large balloon-shaped sail flown at the bow of a yacht when running before the wind.

clue.text: Nation remains in turmoil that everyone can see cracks

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so one letter goes inside the rest
turmoil is confusion and disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A country stays in chaos, and its cracks are visible to the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like the verb 'stays', but it is the anagram material; U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Suriname is a small country on the northern coast of South America, formerly the Dutch colony of Surinam.

clue.text: Polish player, winger

parts.note: to sand is to smooth or polish a surface
a piper is someone who plays the pipes

explanation.surface: A footballer from Poland who plays out on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' wants to be the nationality; it is the verb, and 'winger' is not a footballer but anything with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger is crossword slang for a bird, and the sandpiper is a long-billed wading bird of shorelines.

clue.text: Goddess marrying that male and Egyptian god

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male person
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A goddess weds a man and an Egyptian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marrying' simply joins the goddess to her wordplay, fitting since she presides over marriage; Ra is the sun god of ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus and protector of marriage, which suits the surface.

clue.text: Performer carrying bomb, bully

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a doer is one who performs actions
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: An entertainer smuggling an explosive device is a menacing thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performer' suggests an actor, but it is a DOER, someone who performs a task; 'bully' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone and to domineer over them both mean to control others by arrogant, overbearing intimidation.

clue.text: Religious student, he is apprehended by whippersnapper

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: someone apprehended is seized and held, so this piece is captured inside another

parts.note: a whippersnapper is a cheeky young person, a brat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young seminarian is arrested by an insolent youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'is' goes inside BRAT; 'he' stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebraist is a scholar of the Hebrew language and texts, typically in connection with biblical or Jewish religious study.

clue.text: Natural olfactory sensor, evidently always at the front?

definitions.text: Natural olfactory sensor, evidently always at the front?

indicators.note: the front of each word is its first letter, so the initials are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A sense organ for smell that always leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its initials give the answer, and the organ literally sits at the front of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ for smelling is a built-in sensing device, and it projects forward from the middle of the face.

clue.text: Jargon written about kitchen equipment in contract

indicators.note: written around something means wrapped round it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: cant is the specialised jargon of a group
an oven is a piece of kitchen equipment

explanation.surface: Legal gobbledygook about appliances appears in an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written about' reads as describing a topic, but it means wrapped around: the jargon encloses the appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement, especially a deed or promise between parties, so it is a contract.

clue.text: Lament flash inside head

indicators.note: one thing within another, so a piece sits in the middle of a larger one

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
a mo is a moment, as in 'in a flash'

explanation.surface: Grieving over a sudden flash of pain in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' is a very short time, MO, and 'head' is the slang BEAN, as in to bean someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament something and to bemoan it both mean to express sorrow or complaint about it.

clue.text: Nation featured between covers of riotous book

indicators.note: something featured between two things sits in the middle of them
the covers of something are its outside edges, so its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
Oman is a nation on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A country appears between the covers of a wild novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' here is a book of the Bible, not a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans is the Epistle to the Romans, Paul's letter, one of the books of the New Testament.

clue.text: Topping riddle: about the fourth from Sphinx

parts.note: to riddle with holes, as with bullets, is to pepper
on means about or concerning

indicators.note: the fourth from a word means counting along to its fourth letter and keeping only that

parts.note: S, P, H, I: the fourth letter of the word

explanation.surface: The best riddle is the one about the Sphinx, famous for its riddles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' is not a puzzle but the verb for puncturing all over, as with shot; 'Topping' is pizza topping, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is the spicy sausage sliced over pizzas, one of the commonest toppings on them.

clue.text: Amendment, one being carried

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clause added to a bill or document
second meaning: someone carried along on a horse, bike or vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried' suggests a motion carried by a vote, which fits 'Amendment'; the second meaning is a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an extra clause attached to a legal bill, and also a person borne along on a horse.

clue.text: Turner Prize contradicting itself: so protesting, every second

indicators.note: every second means the second item each time, so the second letter of each word in turn is kept

parts.note: the second letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: The Turner Prize, famous for provoking protest, seems to undermine itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner Prize' reads as the famous British art award, but the definition stops at 'Turner'. The Turner Prize is an annual award for contemporary British art, often controversial.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as a turbine or helicopter, so it is something that turns.

clue.text: Image daubed on spear

indicators.note: daubed means smeared messily, so the letters are smudged into another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A picture smeared on to a weapon, like warpaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Image' sounds like a picture to be painted on, but it means a public face.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is the image or character a person presents to the public, as opposed to their private self.

clue.text: Not for losers, it breaks European record

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece enters another

parts.note: a list is a record of items
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sporting star smashes a European record; the achievement is not for those who lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks … record' suggests an athlete beating a best time, but 'breaks' only means gets inside, splitting the record after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitist attitudes favour a select, superior few and exclude everyone else, so they are not for life's losers.

clue.text: Skirts of raffia, that fibre

indicators.note: the skirts of something are its fringes, so only its outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
yon is an old word for that, as in yonder

explanation.surface: Grass skirts made of raffia, that plant fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like the garments made of raffia, but it means the edges of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile fibre made from regenerated cellulose, often used as a silk substitute.

clue.text: Structure associated with sick people — the rack?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a frame for carrying the ill or injured
second meaning: the torture device that pulls a victim's limbs

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes the rack sound like a hospital fitting; it is the medieval torture frame that elongates its victims.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramedics carry patients on a portable frame, and the rack is a device that lengthens a body by pulling.
